title: Mark paywalled links on Hacker News
question: How can I tell which Hacker News links are paywalled?
answer: Hacker News does not mark paywalled links; the only hint is the site name in brackets after each title. The usermods script on this page adds a small red paywall tag next to stories from sites that keep most articles behind a paywall, such as nytimes.com, wsj.com, ft.com, bloomberg.com and economist.com. The list is in the script and you can edit it. Without a script, check the site name before clicking, or look in the comments, where readers often post an archive link.
prompt: On Hacker News, put a paywall tag next to links from sites like the NYT, WSJ and FT.
details:
The script reads the site name Hacker News prints after each title (`span.sitestr`) and compares it with a fixed list of about 30 paywalled sites, subdomains included. Matching stories get a red `paywall` tag after the site name. Nothing is hidden and the script makes no network requests, so it cannot tell a free article on a paywalled site from a locked one.

The check loads the list of New York Times stories at `from?site=nytimes.com`. The same code runs on the front page, `newest`, `best` and other story lists.

alternatives.title: Archive links in the comments
alternatives.body: Hacker News allows paywalled articles when there is a workaround, and readers often post an archive.today or Wayback Machine link as one of the first comments.

evidence.note: Hacker News Anti-Paywall (total installs, read from api.greasyfork.org/en/scripts/by-site)
returns the query; suggestions: hacker news paywall
HN thread: Is there any way HN can implement a 'paywall tag' to save wasted clicks?
HN thread: Should we use [paywall] tag where applicable?

check.baseline: (() => { const s = [...document.querySelectorAll('.titleline .sitestr')]; return s.length >= 10 && s.every((e) => e.textContent.trim() === 'nytimes.com') && !document.querySelector('.um-paywall'); })()
check.expect: (() => { const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('tr.athing')].filter((r) => r.querySelector('.sitestr')); return rows.length >= 10 && rows.every((r) => { const t = r.querySelector('.titleline .um-paywall'); return !!t && t.checkVisibility() && t.textContent === 'paywall'; }); })()
check.intact: (() => { const links = [...document.querySelectorAll('.titleline > a')].filter((a) => a.checkVisibility() && /nytimes\.com/.test(a.href)); return links.length >= 10 && document.querySelectorAll('.subline').length >= 10; })()
